description: Unload session scripts and attempt to detach REA's Frida session. Then resume a still-paused spawned process if script cleanup or session detach confirms instrumentation was released. Cleanup failures are reported. REA never kills the target; its final state is reported as unknown.

name: instrument_with_frida
title: Instrument With Frida
description: Run caller-authored Frida JavaScript against a selected process for one observation window, then detach. Scripts can read/change target memory and behavior and use the process's capabilities. CLI and MCP share this ephemeral workflow; use start_frida_session/load_frida_script for a persistent session. Remote authentication is call-local and excluded from Evidence. Detachment does not establish target termination.

name: inspect_apktool_client
title: Inspect Apktool Client
description: Inspect the caller-selected apktool launcher: resolved command, selection source, and version. Decodes nothing. REA never installs Apktool or Java; select a launcher with REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND (absolute) or apktool on PATH.

name: decode_android_resources
title: Decode Android Resources
description: Decode APK resources with apktool d --no-src: readable manifest, version/SDK facts, string resources/locales and decoded file count. Uses a temporary workspace removed after projection; smali/source recovery belongs to JADX. Strings default to 2000 valid entries per table; use string_offset/string_limit and table.page.next_offset for later pages, checking target.sha256 across calls. Per-call string budgets can be raised without restart. decode_timeout_ms controls decoding (default 600000 ms), independently of output capture and version probes.

name: inspect_jeb_client
title: Inspect Jeb Client
description: Inspect the running JEB client serving MCP: engine version, GUI or headless mode, and startup time. Does not open a target. Requires a caller-started JEB client reachable at REA_JEB_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8425/mcp); REA never installs or launches JEB.

name: open_jeb_project
title: Open Jeb Project
description: Open or create a JEB project from an artifact file or existing .jdb2 database on the engine host. Returns the project's input-file digests and top-level units. The engine analyzes the target itself; REA does not read the file or execute it. Fails when a project is already open.

name: list_jeb_units
title: List Jeb Units
description: List project units by stable unit path and type, with optional wildcard filter, parent restriction, and pagination. The engine caps pages at 100 units; a full page reports partial coverage because more units may exist. Read-only.

name: decompile_jeb_item
title: Decompile Jeb Item
description: Decompile one type or method to engine pseudo-code using its decompiler (Dalvik, Java, or native). item_address comes from the engine's code item listing; unit_path defaults to the engine's first code unit and stays unknown when omitted. Read-only with respect to the target file.

name: inspect_adb_client
title: Inspect Adb Client
description: Inspect the caller-selected adb client: resolved binary, version, and install path. Never contacts devices and never starts the adb server. REA never installs platform tools; select a binary with REA_ADB_PATH (absolute) or adb on PATH.

name: list_adb_devices
title: List Adb Devices
description: List attached devices exactly as `adb devices -l` reports them: serial, state, transport, model metadata, and an inferred emulator/physical kind with its evidence basis. Emulators and USB or network devices appear alike; REA neither starts nor manages them. transport_id_text preserves exact full-range transport identity; transport_id is its safe numeric projection or null. May start the local adb server on first use.

name: inspect_adb_device
title: Inspect Adb Device
description: Inspect one device's build identity through a fixed `getprop` whitelist: Android and SDK versions, security patch, fingerprint, product identity, CPU ABIs, and debuggable flag, plus the observed emulator indicator ro.kernel.qemu. Present properties retain empty values; omitted keys were not reported. Read-only with respect to the device.

name: list_adb_packages
title: List Adb Packages
description: List installed packages on one device with each base APK's device path, optionally scoped to third-party or system packages. Paths are device filesystem paths, not host-local. Read-only.

name: pull_adb_package
title: Pull Adb Package
description: Pull one installed package's complete APK set (base plus every split, as `pm path` reports) from the device into a caller-selected output directory, creating a package-named subdirectory that must not already exist. Every pulled file is digested with SHA-256; partial pulls keep successful artifacts and per-file failure reasons. The device keeps the originals.

name: read_adb_logcat
title: Read Adb Logcat
description: Read a bounded dump of the device log (`logcat -d -t`) for one buffer, optionally restricted to a process id. No streaming, no clearing; the newest lines are kept when the count cap trims. Read-only.

name: inspect_adb_package
title: Inspect Adb Package
description: Inspect installed-package versions, install times, installer, user id, flags, and requested-permission count through read-only `dumpsys package`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in bounded numeric_issues and make coverage partial; version_code stays exact text. Unknown sections are not inferred.

name: pull_adb_file
title: Pull Adb File
description: Pull one absolute device path (a database, shared-preferences XML, or any readable file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it with SHA-256. The local copy must not already exist. Read-only with respect to the device.

name: push_adb_file
title: Push Adb File
description: Push one local file to an absolute device path. If the destination is an existing directory, adb places the file inside it under the local basename and the result reports that file path. A device-mutating tool: checks for an existing destination file before transfer and refuses it unless overwrite is explicitly requested; this check is not atomic and another process can create the path before adb writes. The private staged copy remains non-writable and preserves source executable bits. When the device provides sha256sum, the transfer is verified by comparing it with the local digest.

name: capture_adb_screen
title: Capture Adb Screen
description: Capture one frame of the device screen as a PNG (`screencap -p` through exec-out, no device-side file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it and reporting its dimensions. No recording or interaction.

name: list_adb_processes
title: List Adb Processes
description: List running processes exactly as `ps -A` reports them: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, and name. Useful for pairing with instrumentation lanes. Read-only.

name: list_adb_directory
title: List Adb Directory
description: List the immediate children of one absolute device directory, including hidden entries: names, kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, dates, and symlink targets. Names and targets preserve embedded newlines. Recognizes the standard errors for absent paths and denied reads. Read-only.

name: list_adb_features
title: List Adb Features
description: List the device's declared hardware and software features (`pm list features`) for device fingerprinting. Read-only.

name: list_adb_services
title: List Adb Services
description: List the device's binder services with their interfaces (`service list`). Read-only.

name: inspect_adb_display
title: Inspect Adb Display
description: Read physical and override size/density from `wm size` and `wm density`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in numeric_issues with partial coverage; optional values remain null. Required physical-size failures retain partial display facts. Read-only.

name: inspect_adb_window
title: Inspect Adb Window
description: Report the window manager's focus declarations with display context, original lines and explicit summary status. Reads `dumpsys window windows`, falling back to `displays` only when no focus field is declared. Singular fields are unknown for multiple contexts or repeated declarations; inspect focus_contexts for every observation. Read-only; no interaction occurs.

name: read_adb_setting
title: Read Adb Setting
description: Read one settings value (`settings get`) from the system, secure, or global namespace. Absent keys report the device's own null observation. Read-only; writing settings is not exposed.

name: collect_adb_bugreport
title: Collect Adb Bugreport
description: Collect one device-generated bugreport archive (`adb bugreport`) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting the zip. The archive contains the device's own dumpstate, dumpsys, and logcat report; collection can take minutes. Read-only with respect to configuration.

name: resolve_adb_packages
title: Resolve Adb Packages
description: Find installed packages by case-insensitive package-name substring and return each base APK device path. Pass an exact returned name to pull_adb_package to retrieve its base and split APKs. Read-only.

name: install_adb_package
title: Install Adb Package
description: Install one local APK on the device (`adb install [-r]`), recording the APK's host digest and byte size. A device-mutating tool: `replace_requested` records whether `-r` was selected; `replaced` is null because install success does not establish prior package state. The device's own Success/Failure verdict is preserved with its reason.

name: uninstall_adb_package
title: Uninstall Adb Package
description: Request package removal for user 0 (`adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`) without data retention. A device-mutating tool; absent packages report the device's own refusal reason.

name: start_adb_app
title: Start Adb App
description: Start one installed app's resolved launcher activity with `am start -W -n`. A device-mutating tool for dynamic analysis. The full wait report determines success; failures retain launch-attempt facts and raw output. Pair with `read_adb_logcat` (pid filter) and `list_adb_processes` to observe the app, and `stop_adb_app` to end the run.

name: start_adb_activity
title: Start Adb Activity
description: Start an intent with `am start -W`: one action, optional data URI, optional explicit component, and up to 16 typed extras (string, boolean, int, long, float). A device-mutating tool; the full wait report determines success, with failed-attempt facts and raw output retained.

name: stop_adb_app
title: Stop Adb App
description: Force-stop every process of one package (`am force-stop`), ending a dynamic-analysis run. A device-mutating tool; it succeeds whether or not the package had running processes.

name: list_browser_targets
title: List Browser Targets
description: List pages exposed by one loopback Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint, optionally filtered by exact origin. Returns target IDs and URLs; query values and fragments are preserved, with URL userinfo credentials removed. Use a returned target ID with inspect_web_page. discovery_timeout_ms controls discovery; command_timeout_ms does not apply. Browser-socket endpoints remain shared by the active browser provider until it closes or target-session cleanup is unconfirmed; cancellation/deadline on a clean socket releases only this call’s lease.

name: inspect_web_page
title: Inspect Web Page
description: Passively inspect one selected page target through CDP without evaluating JavaScript, navigating, clicking, closing, or mutating the page. If no origin filter is supplied, capture is scoped to the target's current origin. Returns DOM structure, accessibility, scripts, resources, attach-window network and console metadata, workers, and redacted storage inventory as Evidence.

name: analyze_web_bundle
title: Analyze Web Bundle
description: Recover a static chunk graph, route/endpoint candidates, vendor fingerprints and page-declared WebMCP metadata from JavaScript on one selected CDP page. May fetch source maps only from the target origin or explicitly selected origins; application JavaScript is not executed. detail summary retains complete Evidence; view {kind: "web-bundle", collection: "endpoints"} selects endpoint rows, and javascript-routes views select route patterns/occurrences/sources/unknowns. Read later pages with inspect_analysis_view. Static candidates do not establish runtime reachability or a complete route set.

name: observe_web_session
title: Observe Web Session
description: Arm a CDP observation window of the requested duration while the user operates the page. By default it follows the selected target's current origin; an explicit origin list controls which origins may be retained. Records navigation, redirect, lifecycle, and failure events.

name: discover_webmcp_tools
title: Discover Webmcp Tools
description: Passively inventory every page-registered WebMCP tool and its complete structural input-schema summary using the experimental CDP WebMCP domain. Metadata is page-declared-untrusted; REA never registers or invokes discovered tools.

name: compare_web_captures
title: Compare Web Captures
description: Compare two passive page inspections or two recorded browser scenarios. For passive captures, pass before/after with each complete inspect_web_page normalized_result in inspection and optional complete discover_webmcp_tools normalized_result in webmcp. For scenarios, pass complete normalized_result objects as before_scenario/after_scenario; use exactly one input group. Returns artifact differences and alignment failures. Scenario steps align by exact IDs; optional literal normalization is recorded. HTTP requests and ordered WebSocket streams are compared without inventing stable identities for same-URL connections. Missing or truncated Evidence never proves equality.

name: capture_web_screenshot
title: Capture Web Screenshot
description: Capture the current visible viewport of one configured page as an inline, content-addressed PNG artifact. The operation never scrolls, navigates, or evaluates page JavaScript.

name: compare_web_screenshots
title: Compare Web Screenshots
description: Compare two self-verifying PNG screenshot artifacts with local pixel metrics. Returns exact changed-pixel ratios and channel deltas without OCR or external services.

name: capture_browser_scenario
title: Capture Browser Scenario
description: Drive a browser scenario when passive observation cannot exercise the app. Launch the selected executable or connect to a loopback CDP target; actions can change application state and make network requests. Supply browser, start_url and actions, e.g. {browser:{mode:"launch",executable_path:"/opt/chromium/chrome"},start_url:{url:"https://app.example.test/"},actions:[{step_id:"settle",action:"wait_for_timeout",duration_ms:250}]}. Empty storage and a URL-only final capture are defaults. Request actions use page fetch on the start origin; capture.network independently opts into request_body, response_body and header_values. Credentials and declared secrets are redacted. capture.limits controls retained event/content budgets; omissions identify affected events/transactions. Actions wait for completion or cancellation; per-action timeout_ms bounds a step. Default complete delivery returns Evidence inline. detail summary retains it and returns step outcomes, final/first-unsuccessful accessibility, and counts; inspect_analysis_view kind browser-scenario pages steps, events, transactions and UTF-16 text. Use inspect_web_page for observation without actions.

name: observe_web_execution
title: Observe Web Execution
description: Instrument one selected CDP page for a finite, externally driven precise coverage window. Resets execution counters and prevents optimized execution until stopped. Returns complete nested UTF-16 ranges/counts, independently hashed script text and request initiator associations by session script ID. Does not navigate, click, evaluate selected code or close the externally owned page. Navigation ends document-scoped collection; workers and UI causality remain outside this claim. Emits an actual armed progress notification before external actions.

name: inspect_web_event_listeners
title: Inspect Web Event Listeners
description: Inspect listeners registered directly on the first main-document CSS match in one selected CDP page. Returns event flags, native callback locations, source ownership and exact script text/digests inline. Does not dispatch events, evaluate JavaScript or invoke handlers. Delegated ancestor/framework listeners and execution history remain unknown. Releases REA's object group and transport, preserving the external page.

name: inspect_web_network_capture
title: Inspect Web Network Capture
description: Inspect a saved local HAR 1.2, mitmproxy, Fiddler SAZ or supported aioquic qlog capture without contacting recorded URLs. Returns source-linked records, preserved producer fields, precise numbers, exposed bytes and explicit coverage/limitations; transport credentials and explicitly marked sensitive values are excluded. Use inspect_web_page for a live CDP page. Preserve capture_path exactly as supplied; it names a path on the REA host, not a path to rebase onto the client workspace. Select format; record_ordinals selects records after full decoding and also decodes recognized protobuf/gRPC bodies. Optional protobuf selects body_pointers, framing and a local FileDescriptorSet/message_type; native gRPC and gRPC-web remain distinct, ambiguous readings stay candidates and compressed payloads stay unknown. Default complete delivery is inline. detail summary retains Evidence for inspect_analysis_view kind capture (preview/complete), protobuf (bodies/frames/fields), or qlog; large text/schema values require explicit fields. Qlog supports aioquic 1.5.0 JSON qlog 0.3 and reports STREAM interval unions/endpoint loss declarations, not recovered bodies or proved network loss. SAZ preserves encoded bytes without replay/HAR conversion; encrypted archives are unsupported. Mitmproxy requires caller-supplied mitmdump 12.2.3 on Linux. Malformed or oversized captures return no partial success; browser transaction attribution and HAR text’s original bytes remain unknown.

name: inspect_electron_fuses
title: Inspect Electron Fuses
description: Inspect packaged Electron fuse bytes in one local macOS app bundle, Electron Framework binary, Windows PE executable, or Linux ELF executable. Returns the artifact digest, per-slice wire version, fuse index, version-1 name, state, and raw byte, plus derived implications for Inspector flags, ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, embedded ASAR integrity, and app.asar-only loading. A missing sentinel is unknown fuse state. Reads artifact bytes only and does not modify the selected file or open a runtime target.

name: list_electron_targets
title: List Electron Targets
description: List every Electron file:// page target from a selected loopback CDP endpoint. Local file paths are canonicalized after symlink resolution. Selecting an endpoint exposes every eligible target and its local path metadata.

name: inspect_electron_page
title: Inspect Electron Page
description: Passively inspect one Electron file page by supplying its loopback CDP endpoint and target ID. The provider rechecks that the target currently exists at that endpoint and is a local file page. Returns frames, DOM structure, resource paths, and scripts without evaluating renderer JavaScript or invoking Electron APIs. The selected endpoint exposes every local file page and its metadata to this tool.

name: analyze_javascript_application
title: Analyze Javascript Application
description: Build a static application graph from a local ASAR or extracted JavaScript app without executing it. Supply input_path, e.g. {input_path:"/apps/client",source_paths:["main.js"],detail:"summary"}. Copy source_paths exactly from the inventory, not host-absolute paths inferred from input_path. Returns nodes, edges, semantic relations, integrity contradictions, coverage and unknowns. source_paths limits source analysis to exact inventoried paths without narrowing inventory or artifact identity; dependencies are not implicitly analyzed and unselected sources remain unknown. detail summary reduces delivery, retaining complete Evidence for inspect_analysis_view; it does not reduce analysis. With summary detail, view {kind:"javascript-routes",collection:"routes",offset:0,limit:64} selects static route patterns; static routes do not prove reachability or the complete route set. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue retains untrusted observed bytes and partial coverage. analysis_timeout_ms is a per-source provider budget. A host-only timeout needs a longer client deadline, not that budget; do not repeat unchanged work or assume it stopped. If configuration cannot be edited, report the host setting (Codex: mcp_servers.<server>.tool_timeout_sec, seconds).

name: reconcile_javascript_runtime
title: Reconcile Javascript Runtime
description: Reconcile verified static JavaScript application graphs with existing passive web/Electron CDP, passive V8 Inspector, or provider-owned active Electron Evidence. Active Electron captures contribute an explicitly partial target-only runtime record; they never invent renderer scripts, frames, workers, or execution claims. Exact captured-source digests take priority over caller-declared file/URL mappings; target, frame, script, and worker ambiguity remains explicit, and source-map authority stays separate.

name: capture_electron_scenario
title: Capture Electron Scenario
description: Launch and exercise an owned Electron app when passive CDP/Inspector observation cannot answer the question. REA owns startup/teardown; selected click/wait, renderer reload/crash and synthetic open-url/second-instance actions change runtime behavior. Returns correlated window/WebContents/process/preload/session/navigation/shell/IPC observations without payload values, plus action targets and coverage/truncation. Actions wait for completion or cancellation; a missing click target can remain pending. External shell, navigation, permission, download, popup, updater and OS-integration effects are blocked and recorded. Cleanup failures retain observations with explicit uncertainty. Use inspect_electron_page or observe_javascript_runtime for passive observation.

name: list_javascript_runtime_targets
title: List Javascript Runtime Targets
description: List every eligible Node/Electron V8 Inspector target from an explicit literal-loopback endpoint. Node discovery file locations that cannot be verified are preserved as unresolved reported URLs; they do not prove filesystem identity. Listing does not attach to targets.

name: observe_javascript_runtime
title: Observe Javascript Runtime
description: Passively observe loaded-script and execution-context metadata on one loopback Node/Electron V8 Inspector target, selected by inspector_endpoint and target_id. Presence/attachability and file locations are rechecked; verified file paths stay separate from reported URLs, including distinct query/fragment identities. Parse failures are counted separately from malformed events. REA does not read source, evaluate, pause/resume or instrument execution; imports, EventEmitter activity and Electron IPC remain unknown. Use reconcile_javascript_runtime with static application Evidence. The selected endpoint exposes every target it serves to this tool.

name: inspect_analysis_settings
title: Inspect Analysis Settings
description: Inspect REA's editable runtime admission sizes, deadlines and worker heaps, their bounds, launch values and application points. No active target is required. Filters intersect. If an error already names a setting and its bounds, update_analysis_settings can be called directly. Explicit per-call arguments override runtime defaults. Active worker values are not observed by this configuration view.

name: update_analysis_settings
title: Update Analysis Settings
description: Atomically set or reset editable runtime defaults for new work. Changes survive target close/open but disappear on REA restart; reset restores launch configuration. Follow an error's named setting/bounds directly, then retry after work and cleanup settle; no inspection is needed when they are supplied. Does not change active work, edit files, restart providers, raise client limits or override explicit per-call arguments.

name: inspect_analysis_view
title: Inspect Analysis View
description: Read summaries, selected facts, or pages from completed Evidence without rerunning analysis. Use the producing tool’s retained-view handoff for compatible selectors; the examples here are not exhaustive. Copy normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary into source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Other sources are {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>} or {kind: "evidence-file", path: "<absolute JSON path>", evidence_id?: "<record ID>"}; select an ID for a multi-record bundle. For native pseudocode use {source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}, view: {kind: "native", facet: "pseudocode", offset: 0, limit: 128}}; procedure_pseudo_code parents support this text facet, while other native function facets require analyze_function. Common views: {kind: "summary"} has no facet; {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64} selects artifact paths; {kind: "capture", detail: "preview", offset: 0, limit: 20} pages saved network records; {kind: "managed-members", collection: "methods", offset: 0, limit: 64} pages managed members. Use the producer’s named kind for other families; compact schemas may omit nested shapes, so do not invent selectors. Text offsets/limits use UTF-16 code units; row pages count the selected retained collection. Preserve parent identity, null/unavailable values, source coverage, limitations and unknowns; exhausting pages does not prove complete discovery, runtime use or absence. Smaller pages can resolve delivery limits without repeating analysis; complete parent Evidence remains available for export.

name: export_web_scripts
title: Export Web Scripts
description: Export JavaScript bytes already retained in one local inspect_web_page or capture_browser_scenario JSON capture (normalized result or complete Evidence). Writes scripts and a digest-verified manifest into an absent absolute output_directory. Returns all source URLs, script or transaction/event references, unavailable states, and an analysis_input for analyze_javascript_application when any bytes were exported. Include script sources in inspect_web_page or select capture.network.response_body in scenarios. No refetch or execution. Safe unambiguous URL layouts preserve relative module paths; versions, query variants, inline scripts, and path collisions are isolated with explicit resolution limitations.

name: trace_web_module_imports
title: Trace Web Module Imports
description: Resolve native ES imports/re-exports from one script in a local export_web_scripts manifest. Verifies the selected source digest/size and returns source positions, resolved URLs/errors and every matching captured candidate. URL query/fragment identities remain distinct; computed imports, bundler IDs and execution remain unknown. Supply importer_url when inline/document-base context is unknown and an import_map when needed. Literal resolution requires absolute REA_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE: caller-supplied Chromium runs only a trusted REA resolver stub with page requests fulfilled locally or blocked, without captured app execution or asset refetch. The native deadline is 20 seconds; cleanup may extend it.

name: trace_web_source_location
title: Trace Web Source Location
description: Map one generated position in an exported script through a caller-paired local source map, verifying manifest/script/map byte identities. Returns all equal-position matches, original positions, resolved source URLs and embedded sourcesContent; pairing does not prove deployment authenticity or execution. Lines are one-based, columns zero-based UTF-16; lookup uses the greatest generated position <= requested across lines. Regular maps and inline indexed sections only; external section URLs are unsupported. No network or application execution; decoding uses an owned codec process. Complete delivery is default. detail summary retains Evidence; view {kind:"source-location",collection:"matches",offset:0,limit:64} pages match metadata. source-text additionally requires match_index and pages UTF-16 text. inspect_analysis_view reuses the retained parent; export_evidence_bundle preserves it. source_map_limits changes byte/record/heap admission per call; decode_timeout_ms is separate. Refusals name the exhausted control; cleanup may outlast the deadline.

name: recover_javascript_sources
title: Recover Javascript Sources
description: Recover readable modules from local UTF-8 JavaScript bundles into an absent output_directory, without executing application code. Requires caller-supplied Wakaru ^1.13.0 (verified 1.14.0), Linux x64 and util-linux prlimit. additional_paths includes related chunks, preserving each input’s snapshot/provenance. Returns original/derived digests, extraction ranges, source maps, warnings and analysis_input for analyze_javascript_application. Splitting may fall back to one module; original names and runtime equivalence remain unknown. One worker has a fixed 120-second deadline and bounded input/output/report admission; limit failures are explicit and roll back output.

name: search_guidance
title: Search Guidance
description: Find installed REA workflow guidance by query words. Returns ranked sections, pages and locators for read_guidance_section; every non-generic word must match, with direct section matches ranked before matches spread across children. Reads documentation only, without accessing a target or provider.

name: read_guidance_section
title: Read Guidance Section
description: Retrieve a section selected by search_guidance from the installed REA guidance bundle. Reports stale locators and unavailable bundles explicitly. Returns documentation, not target observations or Evidence.

name: guided_workflows
title: Guided Workflows
description: List or render REA's existing guided workflows. Rendering returns guidance only; it does not inspect targets, start analysis, or change session state.

name: trace_application_feature
title: Trace Application Feature
description: Trace a typed literal seed through every reachable part of an authenticated JavaScript Application Graph supplied as inline Evidence or exact same-session retained references. Original static, native, passive-runtime, inferred, and unknown authorities remain distinct; native addon handoffs never open a provider or execute the application. An optional view returns selected facts and retains the complete trace.

name: trace_javascript_semantics
title: Trace Javascript Semantics
description: Trace static JavaScript data-flow, direct call/return, and closure relations from inline application Evidence or an exact same-session retained reference. Dynamic or unsupported semantics remain explicit unknowns; static reachability never claims runtime execution.

name: compare_application_versions
title: Compare Application Versions
description: Compare two authenticated JavaScript Application Graph versions, supplied inline or by exact retained reference. Returns added, removed, changed, ambiguous and unknown entities with the full changed_from graph. Pairing uses unique exact digest, source-map, structural or semantic-key tiers; no fuzzy or module-ordinal pairing.

name: compare_static_and_observed_endpoints
title: Compare Static And Observed Endpoints
description: Compare static JavaScript endpoints with requests recorded in HAR Evidence, supplied inline or retained; acquires no files, targets or URLs. Returns exact or inferred template pairings and explicit unknowns; root-relative targets need a declared origin. Not-observed requires an exercised origin, all parent records retained and none excluded; it never means hidden, unused or inaccessible. Default summary retains the full comparison for inspect_analysis_view kind endpoint-comparison (static-endpoints, observed-groups, matches); a selected view overrides detail, and detail complete returns all facts. Copies no query strings, fragments, headers or bodies. Sensitive-declaration parents are refused; the 96 MiB representation budget covers source admission and derived state.

name: inspect_api_contract
title: Inspect Api Contract
description: Inspect declared APIs in local OpenAPI JSON or GraphQL SDL without a session, network requests or target execution. OpenAPI 3.0/3.1/3.2 returns inline method/path operations with source pointers; references remain unresolved. format:"graphql-sdl" returns types/fields and optional operations_path bindings, preserving aliases, fragment/spread owners and unknowns without expanding fragments or claiming full operation validation. Default summary retains Evidence; view overrides detail. For HTTP rows use view {kind:"api-contract",collection:"operations",methods:["GET"],limit:20}; GraphQL uses view {kind:"graphql-contract",collection:"references",limit:20}. inspect_analysis_view pages the same retained facts. Source declaration coverage stays separate from page exhaustion; paging does not increase parser allowances. Introspection, runtime behavior and contract comparison are outside scope.

name: inspect_ntfs_journal
title: Inspect Ntfs Journal
description: Inspect USN V2/V3/V4 records from a local acquired NTFS journal with a caller-paired MFT from the same volume. Reads at most 64 MiB per file. Returns source-order events, explicit coverage rows, both SHA-256 identities, and nextFileOffset for another page using the same inputs. V2 MFT references include sequence numbers; opaque V3/V4 IDs remain unresolved. MFT inventory counts are inline by default; select mft_record_limit for up to 32 detailed records, including identity-checked extension attributes and explicit link coverage. V4 returns at most 16 extent samples per event with explicit omissions. History completeness remains unknown. Other journal versions and unverifiable references remain explicit. Reads only the selected acquisition files.

name: inspect_playwright_trace
title: Inspect Playwright Trace
description: Inspect a local Playwright v10 trace ZIP offline, without browser replay or requests to recorded URLs. Returns action boundaries, console/network facts, screenshot/body references and archive/member/line provenance; no cross-stream total order or complete-capture claim. Context options, most action arguments/results, DOM and resource bytes are not analyzed; credentials use HAR/URL projection. Default summary retains supported Evidence. Use view {kind:"playwright-trace",collection:"events",kinds:["network"],limit:10}, or streams/members/diagnostics pages. Text previews cover 256 UTF-16 units; event-text with exact event_id reads further chunks, and fields ["text"] selects full text. Paging does not raise parsing allowances; one archive import is admitted per decoder while retained views remain independent.

name: compare_source_to_bundle
title: Compare Source To Bundle
description: Map committed historical source to an authenticated JavaScript Application Graph. Supply HistoricalSourceGraph inline or as {kind:"file",path:"/absolute/source.json"}, and graph Evidence inline or retained. Uses explicit digest, source-map and path signals to classify unchanged, modified, removed, split, merged, duplicated or unknown; incomplete coverage and ambiguous weak matches never establish absence or force pairing. Candidate signals are opt-in. Omitted view returns the full report; view {kind:"summary"} or {kind:"source-to-bundle",collection:"mappings"} retains it for later inspect_analysis_view pages. Filters intersect, empty filters select none, and page coverage never upgrades source coverage.

name: compare_javascript_export_shapes
title: Compare Javascript Export Shapes
description: Compare static return-property shapes for one exact module/export on each authenticated JavaScript Application Graph, inline or retained. Variants pair only by reciprocal unique literal discriminants. Returns JSON Pointer changes while keeping property presence separate from value resolution: complete property coverage can establish an addition/removal even when values are unresolved. Dynamic values, incomplete coverage and unpaired variants stay unknown. Does not execute JavaScript; runtime behavior needs a separate probe.

name: build_reconstruction_obligation_ledger
title: Build Reconstruction Obligation Ledger
description: Build a deterministic reconstruction-obligation ledger from an authenticated Evidence bundle, reviewed obligations and an explicit reconstruction manifest. Returns the complete ledger, closure digest and typed diagnostics. Duplicate owners, missing cases or parser/type, weak verifier authority, unenumerated claims, contradictions, dependencies and residual unknowns fail closed; static candidates remain candidates.

name: evaluate_reconstruction_coverage
title: Evaluate Reconstruction Coverage
description: Check evidence-backed reconstruction coverage for one named boundary. Missing ownership or inventory is partial; stale, weak, truncated, skipped, unresolved or conflicting verifier proof is unknown. Contradictions, failed proof, missing owners and authority-routing failures fail closed.

name: export_environment_bundle
title: Export Environment Bundle
description: Write an agent environment bundle from capture_browser_scenario Evidence or HAR inspect_web_network_capture Evidence to an absent absolute output_directory whose parent exists. Copies complete capture Evidence, including recorded bodies, and derives replay/state read tools and served/withheld writes with coverage and next-recording hints. Preview the same coverage with inspect_analysis_view kind environment-coverage. dry_run reports without writing but still validates the destination. Uses default template rules, reads only selected Evidence and optional package_tarball, and writes only that directory; no network access. The bundle README explains agentenv use. Destination refusals name this tool; other failures name their export stage.

name: project_android_application_graph
title: Project Android Application Graph
description: Build a static Android application inventory from the authenticated nested inventory Evidence returned by inspect_artifact for an APK. Returns component paths/hashes, runtime-family hints and path-based bridge hypotheses. Does not decode DEX, execute the APK or establish runtime calls.

name: project_apple_application_graph
title: Project Apple Application Graph
description: Build a static Apple application inventory from the authenticated nested inventory Evidence returned by inspect_artifact for an IPA, .app directory, ZIP or DMG. Returns application roots, nested-bundle roles, launchd plists, component paths/hashes, runtime hints and bridge hypotheses. Roles follow path conventions; plist/CMS semantics and runtime calls are not established.

name: project_harmony_application_graph
title: Project Harmony Application Graph
description: Build a static HarmonyOS inventory from the authenticated nested inventory Evidence returned by inspect_artifact for a HAP, HSP or App Pack. Returns packaging hints, component paths/hashes, child packages, runtime hints, unclassified components and path-based N-API bridge hypotheses. Does not decode Ark bytecode, parse manifest semantics or establish runtime calls.

name: start_build_computer
title: Start Build Computer
description: Start a local agentenv computer, installing/downloading app packages as needed; returns computer_id and a first screenshot. Requires Docker and REA_AGENT_ENV_COMMAND. Request sources install from Ubuntu, apt repositories or a .deb URL and add REA from REA_BUILD_COMPUTER_REA_ARCHIVE in a build-only layer. The app starts later: use start_build_capture, or its Applications > Other menu entry when no capture is active. Set source.electron to apply the export launch policy, adding --no-sandbox unless present because the container lacks Chromium user namespaces. Bundle-folder sources run their existing smoke task unchanged. Initial image builds and concurrent agentenv state updates can take minutes. screenshot selects initial region/format/quality. The computer stays reachable until close_build_computer or server shutdown; if failed-start teardown is unconfirmed, use the error's computer_id to retry close_build_computer.

name: act_on_build_computer
title: Act On Build Computer
description: Act on a running build computer with screenshot, click, drag, scroll, type, type_secret, key, wait, reset; actions can change app state. Returns driver content/images and structured results, with each action logged. Points use the latest frame's pixels (take a screenshot first), or space norm on 0..norm_scale; count 2 double-clicks, drag path has 2..50 points, and keys names one W3C chord (ctrl+s is translated). Region screenshots crop the latest frame rather than recapture; use a full screenshot or wait with screenshot true first. After opening a menu/window, wait for its screenshot instead of taking the action's immediate one. type_secret reads the user-created handle file at $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rea/build-secrets/<handle>, or ~/.config/rea/build-secrets/<handle> into a focused masked field: only the handle is recorded and no screenshot is taken, but later screenshots can expose unmasked fields. reset restores seed data through data/reset and relaunches; screenshot_error after reset does not undo it. Other actions forward the driver's arguments unchanged; refusals such as stale frames retain its message. Actions, capture steps and checks run sequentially per computer; different computers run independently.

name: start_build_capture
title: Start Build Capture
description: Launch the app under capture on a request-built computer and return its open-window screenshot. Downloads package lists as the computer user to identify sources; do not open the app from its menu first. Early exit reports code, stderr tail and capture details. Documents are recognized from file names/~/ paths in window titles; supply state_paths when titles name something else. Save the seed through the app, mark_build_checkpoint seed, make and save the requested change, mark end, then stop_build_capture.

name: mark_build_checkpoint
title: Mark Build Checkpoint
description: Checkpoint the running capture under a unique name; returns acknowledged counts and up to 10 changed files. Files named by window titles rank first, then state_paths/open files, with caches last. Mark seed after saving the seed and end after saving the first change. For later tasks, build on the preceding change and mark end-<task name>; mark near-<task name> after saving a near miss that must fail one task check. Duplicate names are refused.

name: stop_build_capture
title: Stop Build Capture
description: Close the captured app and finish its capture. Returns checkpoints, package/sources, limitations and a draft between seed and end when both exist and no declared secret was used. later_drafts contains one draft per later end-<task name>, relative to the preceding end checkpoint. Drafts list owned-path changes, supported before/after structured values, suggested checks and optional unchanged-state guards. Notes explain missing/thin drafts and recovery: add unrecognized documents to state_paths, or make a change saved in a readable file rather than only dconf. After secret use, automatic drafting is withheld; write the tasks manually. Otherwise write each task from its draft in the user's words and pass the tasks to export_build_environment.

name: export_build_environment
title: Export Build Environment
description: Export the stopped capture and given tasks as an agentenv app bundle, seeded at seed. Each task uses its selected end checkpoint (end by default) and its captured near-<task name> when present. The bundle's eval lists every task; verified files are copied to a new/empty host directory. Refuses publication if names or contents contain declared secrets, including UTF-16/hex/base64/URL/gzip forms; errors identify handles and files. Files under the owned paths that changed between the pre-sign-in and post-sign-in checkpoints, and those named in withhold, are withheld from the seed as sign-in or licence state: each becomes a secret setting the deploy takes from an environment variable as the file's bytes in base64, the README says how to fill it, a check may not name it, and REA keeps its bytes as the secret withheld_files names by handle, for start_build_computer's settings when witnessing; a file larger than 48 KiB cannot be withheld. With seed_sign_in, they are seeded instead, which needs a seed_sign_in consent from record_build_consent; every recorded consent ships as consent.json. A check already passing on the seed or a near miss passing every check refuses the whole export, naming the task and reason. Witness each task on a fresh computer with start_build_computer and check_build_task.

name: check_build_task
title: Check Build Task
description: Evaluate saved-state task checks or run a screen_judge through its configured model endpoint on a running exported app. Returns per-check results, settling status and optional witness state. Reads data/get after files settle using exported verifier semantics; screen_judge captures the screen and uses the agentenv runner with three votes per question. Reads every 0.5 s, waits for 3 s of stable bytes, and bounds observation at 15 s; unsettled results use the last completed read, with read_cut for interrupted reads. Witness stages run in order: seed (supply directory to begin recording) must fail a check, after_edit must pass all, near_miss must fail one, and after_reset must restore every seed result. Use the task prompt alone for the edit. Seed rejects exported task/verifier mismatches. Unreadable or truncated views are undecided, not witnessed failures; an undecidable stage is refused for retry. A failed stage or after_reset ends recording and writes witness.json plus recording segments to directory.

name: measure_build_task
title: Measure Build Task
description: Measure how hard an exported bundle's task is for a model: run it in fresh agentenv computers on this host, each solve the bundle's own steps with the agent deployed as the solver on the model, 3 times, then 2 more unless they passed none or all, and keep it in the band when it passes 1 to 3 of 5. A solve that did not finish is run again, at most twice, and not counted. Before each solve REA stops if the largest cost so far would take the total past budget_usd; a solve's cost is known only when it ends, so the first always runs, and a solve that reports no cost stops the measure. The solver calls the model endpoint agentenv reads where REA starts: LITELLM_BASE_URL and LITELLM_API_KEY, or [model] in .agentenv/config.toml; REA holds no model client and never reads the key. It writes difficulty.json at the bundle's root, each measured task's record by name, and a Measured difficulty section in its README, and returns the record: the band, passes, finished solves (k), turns, cost, failures per check and each solve. Solves run one at a time and take minutes each; REA reports progress meanwhile.

name: record_build_consent
title: Record Build Consent
description: Record a consent the person gave, in their own words, after you asked them: kind licence when they accepted a licence the app or its installer shows, which you then accept on their behalf, or seed_sign_in when they allowed the bundle to hold their sign-in or licence state. Never record one they did not give. The consent is kept with the computer; the export writes every one into the bundle's consent.json, and seeds withheld state only with a seed_sign_in consent.

name: close_build_computer
title: Close Build Computer
description: Tear down a build computer and discard its state, cancelling its active call and refusing queued calls. Tries agentenv first, then REA_DOCKER_COMMAND on only that sandbox's named/labelled containers. Unconfirmed teardown reports remaining resources and retains the computer for another close attempt.

name: open_bundle_resources
title: Open Bundle Resources
description: Open a local app bundle for read-only plist, Interface Builder, asset catalog, and keyed archive inspection without resolving or inventing its executable identity. This switches the shared session to a resource-only lane; executable analysis is unavailable until another target is opened.

name: open_binary
title: Open Binary
description: Open a validated local artifact or analysis database and bind its analysis provider. Switching target/provider can discard ephemeral Ghidra edits even if the later open fails; retained investigation Evidence does not restore them. Reopening the same target/profile retains the engine and edits. provider_id selects a provider or deterministic auto routing, with no failure fallback. Omitted format uses headers; format dos-com admits 1..65280 headerless bytes, while raw-binary requires architecture and entry_point and maps file offset 0 there. Optional snapshots must match target, provider and analysis profile; close/reopen before importing into a mutated engine. For Ghidra cross-process edits, set a private absolute REA_GHIDRA_CHECKPOINT_DIR at startup (stock ELF/PE/Mach-O on Linux/macOS); normal opens/closes restore/save metadata. Failed opens report selection_at_failure and target/provider at completion; use binary_session for current state. close_binary releases engine resources; reset_investigation clears retained records.

name: close_binary
title: Close Binary
description: Release the active engine and owned resources while retaining investigation Evidence and complete Unknown history in memory. Drains earlier requests and queues later ones. If cleanup fails, keep this connection and retry close_binary without snapshot_path after the reported condition settles. Optional snapshot_path saves a target-bound snapshot first; resource-only sessions have no snapshot binding, existing files require overwrite, and failed saves keep the engine open. Metadata edits prevent immutable snapshot saves until recreation. Ghidra checkpoint mode saves metadata on normal close and retains the Program for retry if saving fails. Closing does not persist investigation records: export_evidence_bundle to save them, or reset_investigation to clear them.

name: reset_investigation
title: Reset Investigation
description: Discard retained Evidence and Unknown revision history, including engine replay/source bindings, while keeping a healthy active engine open. Drains earlier work and queues later requests. Optional save_path atomically syncs and publishes a complete bundle first; import_evidence_bundle restores its IDs/history. Cancellation, failed save or incomplete cleanup preserves records; any already-published checkpoint is reported. Without save_path, records are lost. binary_session reports the representation budget; no automatic persistence or eviction occurs.

name: binary_session
title: Binary Session
description: Inspect current target, provider capabilities, analysis and server identity without starting analysis. Default summary reports Ghidra checkpoint/ephemeral mode in capabilities[].shared_limitations; detail complete adds diagnostics, candidate capabilities and tool flags. Set refresh_candidates true to recheck provider readiness without changing the active engine. analysis_provider_candidates_observed distinguishes fresh observations from selection-time facts. open_binary with provider_id can replace the engine and discard ephemeral edits; reopening without it reuses the route. release_verification is optional reported-version evidence, not executable authentication. omitted_fields names facts left out of summary.

name: export_evidence_bundle
title: Export Evidence Bundle
description: Atomically write the session's deterministic Evidence bundle to the requested local path. Existing files require overwrite: true; records and manifests use canonical byte-stable ordering.

name: import_evidence_bundle
title: Import Evidence Bundle
description: Read the JSON bundle at the supplied local path, validate every Evidence ID and canonical manifest, then atomically merge it. Imported content is data only and is never executed. Import restores registry entries present in the bundle; questions embedded in Evidence do not automatically become Unknown registry entries.

name: get_evidence_bundle
title: Get Evidence Bundle
description: Read retained Evidence and tracked questions without rerunning providers. Default complete returns an importable canonical bundle. detail summary lists record metadata; records pages complete records with unchanged IDs and missing direct evidence_links, but is not an importable bundle. detail links inspects retained/missing links without payloads; traversal retained-closure follows retained links and defaults to missing rows. Summary/records/links filters accept Evidence ID, operation, target SHA-256, analysis-profile digest or canonical procedure address. Metadata keeps retention distinct from truncated/unavailable source coverage. Use a discovered evidence_id with a compatible inspect_analysis_view to read selected facts.

name: capture_process_scenario
title: Capture Process Scenario
description: Run a caller-selected command under a PTY and return process capture Evidence and unknowns. It runs with the user's permissions, can change files or use network, and is not a sandbox. dry_run validates and returns a rea.process-scenario-plan without launching. Command names use inherited PATH; cwd defaults to the caller's and environment overrides augment inheritance. Filesystem observation is opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. Terminal size must satisfy columns × (rows + scrollback) <= 1,000,000 on every resize; dimensions are never clamped and this limit has no override. Environment keys reject =/NUL and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved. With positive finalization_ms, timeout/idle sends identity-checked SIGTERM, observes until the interval ends, then sends SIGKILL once; exit.finalization records attempts and observed exit. Cancellation still ends the run immediately.

name: compare_process_captures
title: Compare Process Captures
description: Compare compatible process captures, inline or by {kind:"retained-evidence",evidence_id}, across terminal, interaction, lifecycle, process, filesystem, command-shim, HTTP and WebSocket observations. Optional trace_spec checks explicit partial-order or finite-trace assertions, including selected timing. Observer timing alone does not establish changed behavior; timestamps or sorting never establish concurrency. Missing, journal-free or truncated observations never establish equivalence.

name: compare_artifacts
title: Compare Artifacts
description: Compare complete artifact inventories by occurrence path, content identity, metadata and graph relations; root . identifies the outer container separately. Accepts complete inline Evidence, {kind:"retained-evidence",evidence_id} for inspect_artifact/nested inventory/retained summary, or {kind:"evidence-file",path:"/absolute/bundle.json"} with optional evidence_id. Summaries resolve to their complete parent in that session/source bundle; summary facts alone are insufficient. Returns every delta inline with both source identities; coverage gaps remain truncated or unknown, never equivalence. Includes FIT and legacy uImage components.

name: compare_functions
title: Compare Functions
description: Compare two explicit analyze_function Evidence records or exact retained session references across identity, exact provider text, calls, references, strings, and address-normalized CFG topology. The same authenticated Evidence record or compatible same-artifact entry coordinates establish correspondence independently of symbol origin; metadata and text changes remain separate. Missing or provider-incompatible facets remain truncated or unknown; every conclusion cites both Evidence sets.

name: match_native_functions
title: Match Native Functions
description: Pair two retained list_procedures inventories by unique exact symbols, then unique identical observed bytes. Optional same-context name/body/byte/dossier Evidence adds static facts; compatible CFG/call/string fingerprints propose unresolved groups only. Duplicate candidates stay unresolved, and only_left/right means unpaired within inputs, not proven addition/removal. Default summary retains the full matching for function-matches pages; complete returns every group. byte-sources identifies selected read_bytes Evidence: intersect IDs with function evidence_links. Dossier pairs supply retained-reference compare_functions inputs.

name: compare_bundles
title: Compare Bundles
description: Compare two canonical Evidence bundles by exact record membership, explicit one-to-one observation pairs, and complete residual-unknown revision histories. Supply absolute local filesystem paths; relative paths are rejected. Missing bundle members describe omission only, never behavioral equivalence; output is digest-anchored and returns every change inline.

name: find_changed_behavior
title: Find Changed Behavior
description: Aggregate validated process, artifact, and function comparison Evidence, supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references from this session. Original records and their complete source closure remain authenticated; summaries do not substitute for comparisons. Runtime observations remain distinct from static behavior candidates; missing or incomplete comparisons produce unresolved findings, never causal claims. Returns every finding inline.

name: build_call_path
title: Build Call Path
description: Build every shortest direct-callee path from complete analyze_function Evidence supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references. References reuse the complete parent of an analyze_function summary without resending dossiers. Uses exact canonical addresses; missing dossiers and provider mixing remain unknown, and every node and edge cites source Evidence.

name: correlate_static_and_runtime
title: Correlate Static And Runtime
description: Evaluate every explicit caller-declared hypothesis between static and runtime comparison Evidence supplied inline or by exact retained-evidence references. Similar names or paths are never auto-matched, consistent cochange never proves causality, and unknown or truncated inputs remain unresolved. Returns all correlations and their complete Evidence closure inline.

name: verify_reconstruction
title: Verify Reconstruction
description: Verify a finite typed behavioral and structural specification against a canonical Evidence bundle. Pass means every declared claim has complete comparable authority—not global source equivalence; changed claims fail and missing, limited, or unresolved evidence stays unknown.

name: list_unknowns
title: List Unknowns
description: List tracked questions' current revisions in deterministic ID order, with exact status/severity/domain filters. Complete inline by default; offset/limit pages the filtered order, total counts matches and next_offset null means exhausted. Unresolved, contradicted and non-truth dispositions stay distinct. An empty registry does not mean retained Evidence has no residual questions; inspect that Evidence or its analysis view.

name: record_unknown
title: Record Unknown
description: Create one deterministic residual unknown and immutable mutation evidence. Its scope is the active binary analysis target digest, or null without an active target; supporting Evidence does not select the scope. Scope contributes to stable identity. Validates all evidence and relationship references, and rejects duplicate stable identity.

name: update_unknown
title: Update Unknown
description: Append a full-state revision to one tracked question, with immutable mutation Evidence. Requires exact expected_revision; stale writers fail rather than overwrite. The question keeps its original scope, while mutation Evidence uses the active target digest or null and can have a different subject.

name: verify_unknown_resolution
title: Verify Unknown Resolution
description: Check a tracked question's current resolution against bundled Evidence, required authority/confidence/environment and revision integrity. Withdrawn and out-of-scope dispositions do not establish truth.

name: get_navigation_context
title: Get Navigation Context
description: Return the selected document, current address, and containing/current procedure in one provider-neutral result. The result reflects sequential provider observations, not an atomic cursor snapshot; a cursor outside any procedure returns procedure: null.

name: inspect_address_context
title: Inspect Address Context
description: Inspect one explicit reproducible address for its analyzed name, containing procedure, regular and inline comments, and matching bookmarks. Each unsupported facet returns a typed unavailable outcome. A facet rejected for invalid input, source Evidence integrity, or a resource constraint retains its canonical error and recovery alongside successful facets. Use xrefs, assembly, or pseudocode for those deeper views.
